title: Replace agentic.nvim with codecompanion.nvim (ACP, claude_code + opencode)
description: ai_assistant.lua configured carlos-algms/agentic.nvim with the opencode-acp provider. Replaced it with olimorris/codecompanion.nvim, using its ACP interaction by default, restricted to exactly two ACP providers: claude_code and opencode (adapters.acp.opts.show_presets=false plus explicit claude_code/opencode entries via adapters.extend). Kept equivalent keybindings under the <leader>a* namespace, renaming <leader>ad to <leader>aD to avoid an existing collision with a telescope Anki-deck picker mapping, and dropping the old agentic-widget-specific focus-toggle hack (<leader>af) since CodeCompanion's chat buffer is a normal window reachable via standard <C-w> navigation.
close_reason: Replaced carlos-algms/agentic.nvim with olimorris/codecompanion.nvim in lua/core/plugins/ai_assistant.lua. Configured adapters.acp with show_presets=false and explicit claude_code/opencode entries only; interactions.chat.adapter defaults to opencode (ACP). Verified via headless nvim that lazy.nvim installs/loads the plugin, the resolved config matches (default adapter=opencode, acp keys={claude_code,opencode}), :CodeCompanionChat/:CodeCompanionActions commands exist, and all new keymaps (<leader>ac/<leader>an/<leader>aC/<leader>aD/<C-a>) register in the correct modes without colliding with existing mappings. lazy-lock.json updated minimally (agentic.nvim removed, codecompanion.nvim added) after reverting an unrelated bulk plugin-update side effect from testing.

title: Add CodeCompanion session-resume keybinding
description: Add a keybinding that opens a fresh Copilot ACP chat and submits CodeCompanion's /resume command so saved sessions can be restored without manual entry.
close_reason: Added <leader>ar to open a fresh Copilot ACP chat and auto-submit /resume.

title: Make inbox target file a fallback chain, not a single hardcoded file
description:
M.append_to_inbox() in lua/core/plugins/markdown/lists.lua currently always writes to a single hardcoded path: <obsidian_root>/lists/inbox.md. Instead, it should try a list of candidate inbox files in priority order and append to the first one that exists/qualifies, with the current lists/inbox.md becoming the LAST fallback in that chain (i.e. still always works even if nothing else applies).

Needs design/clarification with user during implementation:
- What are the other candidate files in the fallback chain (e.g. a daily note, a project-specific inbox, etc.)?
- What determines whether a candidate 'qualifies' (existence? some marker?).
- Should M.open_inbox() (which opens rather than appends) follow the same fallback logic?
design: Likely needs a small ordered list of path-resolution functions tried in sequence, falling through to the existing lists/inbox.md behavior as the final case.
acceptance_criteria: append_to_inbox and (if applicable) open_inbox resolve the target file via an ordered fallback list instead of a single hardcoded path; existing behavior (lists/inbox.md) still works when no other candidate matches.
close_reason: Implemented fallback chain: <root>/memory/gtd/inbox.md first, falling back to existing <root>/lists/inbox.md; open_inbox now follows the same resolution.
